A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations measuring parameter, voltage, and spatial recovery for simplified neurons and reconstructed RGC and CA1 morphologies, plus runtime experiments.

after.justification: V2 reports original simulation results for these neuron models, including comparisons of covariance approximations, reconstruction results, and analyses of approximation failure.

M1.justification: V2 revises the stated observation model: transmembrane current includes surface area and capacitive current, yielding a voltage-only linear observation mapping (Section 2). It also introduces a block-diagonal EKF with dense voltage covariance and diagonal gating covariance, substantially extending v1's full and diagonal EKF procedures.

E1.justification: The simulated extracellular-inference tasks and RGC/CA1 morphology coverage remain. V2 adds explicit high- versus low-frequency spiking scenarios in a 100-compartment cable analysis (Figure B.2), extending the tested dynamical regimes. Changes in compartment counts within existing validation tasks are principally experimental-setting changes.

E2.justification: The simple-model comparison expands from EKF versus MSE fitting to full EKF, diagonal EKF, block-diagonal EKF, and MSE (Figure 2C). V2 also adds diagonal-versus-full EKF comparisons for the multi-branch model and diagonal-versus-block-diagonal comparisons for RGC, substantially broadening the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes from one compartment, 10 µm electrode distance, and 3 µV baseline noise to ten compartments, 5 µm, and 1 µV. Multi-branch injected current changes from 0.5 to 2 nA. RGC uses 10 rather than 169 electrodes and replaces the 0.1/10 µV sweep with low-noise experiments. CA1 noise changes from 1 to 0.1 µV and fitting switches from full to block-diagonal EKF.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial approximation-validity analyses: firing-regime Jacobian heatmaps, measurement-coupling heatmaps, and diagonal-EKF parameter, voltage, and localization diagnostics (Appendix B; Figures E.2 and E.6–E.9). RGC becomes an explicit approximation-failure comparison. V1's RGC noise-sensitivity sweep is removed; the channel-misspecification tests and runtime analysis remain, with the former using revised setups.

E5.justification: V2 no longer reports the RGC ten-dataset replication and associated mean/standard-deviation summaries shown in v1's Appendix D. It reports over 100 RGC initializations instead of 100. Forty-dataset uncertainty reporting for simpler models remains. Missing replication reporting does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: V2 adds results showing block-diagonal EKF matching full EKF/MSE while diagonal EKF exhibits bias (Figure 2C). RGC results change from successful diagonal-EKF recovery to diagonal failure and block-diagonal success (Figure 4). CA1 recovery traces are replaced, with remaining errors emphasized for leak conductances. These involve changed formulations or settings, so they do not establish same-setting performance gains; the approximately twofold diagonal-EKF runtime result is retained.

T1.justification: V2 revises the transmembrane-current definition and derives the linear observation mapping. New Appendices B and C analyze Jacobian sensitivities and electrode coupling, define the BD(K) covariance family, and prove its closure under stated assumptions, with block update and complexity derivations. The earlier geometric unidentifiability argument is retained in Appendix D.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about extracellular-only biophysical inference, robustness to misspecification, and applicability to reconstructed morphologies remain substantially unchanged. The introduction expands the claimed scalable-inference contribution from diagonal covariance approximation to both diagonal and block-diagonal approximations.

C2.justification: V1 mainly gives generic warnings about approximation bias. V2 identifies concrete validity conditions involving integration steps, gating sensitivities, firing frequency, and electrode–compartment geometry. It explains RGC diagonal-EKF failure through measurement coupling, motivates preserving voltage correlations, and discusses reducing gating variances as a mitigation. These substantially qualify the method's applicability.

D1.justification: V2 newly states the multi-branch axial resistivity, but omits previously specified current-injection amplitudes for misspecification, RGC, and CA1 experiments. Software versions, hardware, and code-access information remain. Reproducibility also suffers from an unresolved discrepancy: Table 1 retains leak conductance 0.003 S/cm² while the revised single-branch plots mark approximately 0.0003 as the true value.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gold, Henze, and Koch (2007), 'Using extracellular action potential recordings to constrain compartmental models,' when defining transmembrane current. The broader literature coverage and first-to-fit positioning remain largely unchanged. Conversion to numbered references is stylistic.

P1.justification: The exposition is substantially reorganized: Section 3.2 separates diagonal approximation, validity, and block-diagonal approximation; experimental passages are rewritten around approximation comparisons; and appendices place validity theory and geometric identifiability before experimental details. The abstract and broad six-section main-text outline remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different conference layout and substantially redesigns the visual presentation. Figure 2 introduces boxplots and rearranged panels; Figure 4 replaces noise/conductance panels with approximation comparisons and a heatmap. Multiple diagnostic figures are added, and RGC noise-sweep displays disappear. Existing localization and runtime figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the scientific foundation by correcting the main-text current formulation and replacing broadly favorable diagonal-EKF evidence with explicit validity conditions, a demonstrated failure case, and an evaluated block-diagonal alternative. These address central modeling and approximation deficiencies. Reduced RGC noise/uncertainty reporting, omitted stimulus amplitudes, and the Table 1/figure discrepancy weaken validation and reproducibility, but the gains in model specification and evidence about approximation limits outweigh those losses.
